question: Something went wrong with this Tamoz runtime in the last few hours. Use the probes to investigate its own record and report the root cause. Set the hypothesis field to exactly one error code identifying the root cause, with no other words or punctuation. Discuss your reasoning and other codes in the findings.

error.message: 402 Payment Required: the account balance is empty

findings.statement: All 5 failed effects in the 6-hour window belong to a single execution on thread.noise.5; every other turn (thread.noise.0 through thread.noise.4) completed cleanly.

Within that execution, 3 model.generate.plan calls and 2 tool.read_file calls succeeded first (1791145349616-1791145349630), then 4 consecutive model.generate.plan attempts failed with Tamoz::Agent::ModelCallError code insufficient_balance (1791145349634-1791145349646). The provider worked and then stopped, which is the signature of the model account's balance being exhausted mid-turn, not a code or graph defect.

The runtime's own rules fired twice, both high severity and both on the same failure: effect.repeated_failure and model.call_failed, category dependency_unavailable, detail Tamoz::Agent::ModelCallError/insufficient_balance. Both rules point at the same code; no rule fired for anything else.

The remaining failure, tool.read_file with ToolError not_found (sha256:6fdfd95b...#1 at 1791145349650), is a one-off local miss that occurred after the model calls had already started failing. It fired no rule, was not repeated, and did not stop the turn, which still reached outcome completed. It is a downstream symptom/noise event, not the root cause.

The code insufficient_balance is a provider/account condition (out of credit), not a Tamoz bug; the action hint on model.call_failed says exactly this. Retrying the plan generation cannot help, and indeed each of the 4 attempts was a distinct effect key failing on attempt 1.

gaps.why: The runtime record shows the error code but not the account balance, the provider, or whether the balance is shared across sessions, so the operator must confirm the credit state with the provider.

gaps.datum: Post-failure activity on thread.noise.5
gaps.why: The turn is marked completed and the record shows no retry or recovery after 1791145349650, but I cannot see what final answer the turn gave or whether the missing plan degraded its output.

gaps.datum: Why thread.noise.5 made 9 effects while sibling threads made fewer
gaps.why: If heavier turns drain credit faster, that would explain why only this execution crossed the balance threshold, but the record does not include per-call cost.

proposals.action: Top up or fix the model provider account (the session profile 'profile:default' in the approval record) and verify the next model.generate.plan succeeds before resuming work.
proposals.rationale: The root cause is a provider balance problem; no code change will fix it, and all four failures are one cause seen four times.

proposals.action: Treat ModelCallError/insufficient_balance as non-retryable and stop the turn's remaining model calls as soon as it is returned, instead of issuing further plan generations that fail.
proposals.rationale: Four separate effect keys each failed on attempt 1 within 12 ms of each other; retrying an exhausted account only adds failed effects to the record.

proposals.action: Keep not_found on tool.read_file as a low-severity event; do not wire it into the repeated-failure rule.
proposals.rationale: It was a single isolated miss that fired no rule and did not affect the outcome, so alerting on it would bury the real signal.

findings.statement: Every failure in the 4-hour window is the same: Tamoz::Agent::ModelCallError with code rate_limited, on operation model.converse.work_step, 8 effects all on thread.noise.5.
The 8 failures are clustered between at_ms 1791145349641 and 1791145349669 (~30 ms apart), each failing on attempt 1 with duration 0-1 ms and no retry — a burst rejected immediately, not a timeout.

On the same thread and immediately before the burst, model.generate.plan (3 effects) and tool.read_file (2 effects) succeeded in ~1 ms each; failures are isolated to one operation type, not the provider generally.

No other error code exists in the record: 38/38 effects accounted for (30 succeeded, 8 failed), 6/6 requests completed, all 6 write_file approvals asked and approved, no unknown outcomes, no logged worker errors, degraded=false.
The other five threads (noise.0 through noise.4) completed cleanly with only approvals and successful effects; the incident is confined to thread.noise.5's work_step calls.

gaps.datum: Whether rate_limited came from the upstream model provider (HTTP 429) or from Tamoz's own client-side concurrency/rate limiter
gaps.why: The recorded failure has only class and code; the burst pattern (8 calls within 30 ms, immediate 0-1 ms rejections) suggests a local limiter, but the record does not distinguish the two.

gaps.datum: Why thread.noise.5 issued 8 concurrent work_step calls after its turn had already completed at ...49619
gaps.why: The effects have request_id=null plus task_ids, i.e. background work outside the request window; the scheduling path that produced the burst is not visible in the probes.

proposals.action: Add exponential backoff with jitter and a retry budget to model.converse.work_step calls, instead of recording a single immediate failure.
proposals.rationale: All 8 effects failed on attempt 1 with 0-1 ms duration; a rate limit is transient and backoff would have absorbed it.

proposals.action: Cap concurrency of work_step model calls per thread (e.g. a small semaphore) so a single thread cannot fire 8 calls in 30 ms.
proposals.rationale: The failures are a tight burst on one thread while identical calls before and on other threads succeeded, which points to self-inflicted rate-limit trips.

proposals.action: Record the upstream status/headers (retry-after, provider id) in ModelCallError so future diagnoses can separate provider 429s from the runtime's own limiter.
proposals.rationale: The stored failure carries only class and code, which is why the source of the limit could not be pinned down from the record.

Summary: Investigated the Tamoz runtime's own record for the last 4 hours via probe_self_diagnose, probe_self_timeline and probe_self_explain_turn. The only failures anywhere in the window are 8 model.converse.work_step effects on thread.noise.5, all failing with Tamoz::Agent::ModelCallError code rate_limited; all other effects, requests and approvals completed normally. Root cause: the model-call rate limiter, error code rate_limited.
Hypothesis (medium confidence): rate_limited
Findings:
1. Every failure in the 4-hour window is the same: Tamoz::Agent::ModelCallError with code rate_limited, on operation model.converse.work_step, 8 effects all on thread.noise.5. [from probe_self_timeline, probe_self_explain_turn]
2. The 8 failures are clustered between at_ms 1791145349641 and 1791145349669 (~30 ms apart), each failing on attempt 1 with duration 0-1 ms and no retry — a burst rejected immediately, not a timeout. [from probe_self_explain_turn]
3. On the same thread and immediately before the burst, model.generate.plan (3 effects) and tool.read_file (2 effects) succeeded in ~1 ms each; failures are isolated to one operation type, not the provider generally. [from probe_self_explain_turn, probe_self_timeline]
4. No other error code exists in the record: 38/38 effects accounted for (30 succeeded, 8 failed), 6/6 requests completed, all 6 write_file approvals asked and approved, no unknown outcomes, no logged worker errors, degraded=false. [from probe_self_diagnose, probe_self_timeline]
5. The other five threads (noise.0 through noise.4) completed cleanly with only approvals and successful effects; the incident is confined to thread.noise.5's work_step calls. [from probe_self_timeline]
Still unknown:
- Full probe_self_diagnose payload (artifact:sha256:90e21e2cc72fcf402646c1f8c61e589bf15474da760438753e73a0ad3cdcbf8b, 15.2 KB on one line): recall_output shows only a truncated preview of the single long line, so the fired-rule ids and per-operation latency/attempt breakdown inside it could not be read directly; the visible summary fields (failed=8, succeeded=30, degraded=false) are consistent with the timeline.
- Whether rate_limited came from the upstream model provider (HTTP 429) or from Tamoz's own client-side concurrency/rate limiter: The recorded failure has only class and code; the burst pattern (8 calls within 30 ms, immediate 0-1 ms rejections) suggests a local limiter, but the record does not distinguish the two.
- Why thread.noise.5 issued 8 concurrent work_step calls after its turn had already completed at ...49619: The effects have request_id=null plus task_ids, i.e. background work outside the request window; the scheduling path that produced the burst is not visible in the probes.
Proposed next actions (not executed; ask for one to run it through approval):
1. Add exponential backoff with jitter and a retry budget to model.converse.work_step calls, instead of recording a single immediate failure.: All 8 effects failed on attempt 1 with 0-1 ms duration; a rate limit is transient and backoff would have absorbed it. [from probe_self_explain_turn]
2. Cap concurrency of work_step model calls per thread (e.g. a small semaphore) so a single thread cannot fire 8 calls in 30 ms.: The failures are a tight burst on one thread while identical calls before and on other threads succeeded, which points to self-inflicted rate-limit trips. [from probe_self_explain_turn, probe_self_timeline]
3. Record the upstream status/headers (retry-after, provider id) in ModelCallError so future diagnoses can separate provider 429s from the runtime's own limiter.: The stored failure carries only class and code, which is why the source of the limit could not be pinned down from the record. [from probe_self_diagnose]

The probes' own record shows six completed turns and 34 effect attempts, of which 30 succeeded and exactly 4 failed — all four are check.test runs on thread.noise.5, each failing with Tamoz::Agent::CheckFailed / check_exit_nonzero. Every other operation in the window succeeded, so the sole error in the runtime's record is the failing test check.
Hypothesis (high confidence): check_exit_nonzero
Findings:
1. All four failures in the window share one class and code: Tamoz::Agent::CheckFailed / check_exit_nonzero, on operation check.test, all in thread.noise.5, execution fdfcaa8e-8104-482c-9c63-0226513cd50a, between 1791145495703 and 1791145495713 ms (~11 ms apart). [from probe_self_explain_turn]
2. Nothing else failed: 18 model.generate.plan attempts and 12 tool.read_file attempts all succeeded with 0 unknown outcomes, and a wider 24-hour window shows identical totals (34 effects, 4 failed, 30 succeeded), so the problem is confined to check.test. [from probe_self_explain_turn, probe_self_timeline]
3. Each failing check.test effect recorded exactly one attempt, failed immediately (durations 0-1 ms), was not retried, and requires no reconciliation; the turn itself still shows outcome completed. This is a deterministic nonzero exit from the check command, not a timeout or a flaky retry pattern. [from probe_self_diagnose]
4. Healthy threads (thread.noise.1 checked directly; the rest via the timeline) completed with successful plan and read_file effects and approve verdicts; the only structural difference in the failing thread is the four check.test effects. All 6 approval decisions in the window were 'approve' — no denials — and the runtime is not degraded (degraded=false, no reasons). [from probe_self_diagnose, probe_self_explain_turn]
Still unknown:
- The check command's stdout/stderr and actual exit status: The probe record stores only the failure class and code; without the check's output the underlying reason the test command exited nonzero (which check, which assertion or missing runner) cannot be confirmed from the record alone.
- Occurrences / logged worker errors in the window: runtime.sqlite3 shows occurrences=0, so there are no worker error log rows to corroborate or contradict the check_exit_nonzero reading.
Proposed next actions (not executed; ask for one to run it through approval):
1. Run the configured test check by hand in the workspace to capture its real exit status and output, then fix that single cause rather than retrying the calls.: The record identifies the failing operation (check.test) but not the command's output; running it manually is the fastest way to see why it exits nonzero. [from probe_self_explain_turn]

Consider surfacing check.test failures as a turn-level failure or operator-visible event instead of recording them only as effect rows.: Thread.noise.5's turn reported 'completed' even though all four of its checks failed, so an operator reading only turn outcomes would miss the incident. [from probe_self_explain_turn, probe_self_diagnose]

findings.statement: Exactly one failure mode exists in the window: 12 tool.read_file effect attempts on thread.noise.5 (1791145495708–1791145495734), all class Tamoz::Agent::ToolError with code path_outside_workspace. No other error class or code appears anywhere in the record.

The burst is the only activity in 24 hours: six turns (thread.noise.0–thread.noise.5) between 1791145495556 and 1791145495734, all requested and completed. Widening the probe window from 4h to 24h returns the identical record, so nothing earlier or later contributes failures.

The diagnose probe's single high-severity finding (rule effect.repeated_failure, category dependency_unavailable) fires on exactly these 12 attempts, and degraded is false with no other findings — the runtime's own diagnosis agrees there is one recurring cause.

On thread.noise.5, two tool.read_file attempts immediately before the burst succeeded (task.df40fab6 at 1791145495701, task.8d5dec3d at 1791145495704), then 12 consecutive reads failed. The reader and workspace root were working seconds earlier; only the requested paths were rejected. Each failure is attempt #1 and never retried.

Everything else succeeded: 18/18 model.generate.plan attempts, the 2 pre-failure reads, and 6 write_file approval decisions all resolved as approve (decision.f19ea059, 385f342f, 9f44433d, cd0f32b0, cac26ad8, 86286b83). The failures are not approval-related, and there are no unknown outcomes, timeouts, or journal drops.

Alternative codes can be excluded by absence and by context: no timeout, rate_limit, unavailable, denied, or unknown-outcome codes occur anywhere in the 24h window, and the two successful reads on the same thread rule out a broken read path or lost workspace root.

gaps.why: The recorded effect attempts and turn decision carry only class and code, not the argument values, so the report cannot say which off-root paths were requested (absolute paths, traversal, or symlink resolution) nor which plan step generated them. gaps.why: The workspace contains no source (list_directory is empty, search for the code has no matches), so the exact resolution rules the guard applies cannot be confirmed from code; the conclusion rests on the runtime record alone.

proposals.action: Investigate what produced the off-root read paths in thread.noise.5 starting at 1791145495708: the model plans succeeded, so check whether the plan output or the caller resolved paths against the wrong base (absolute host paths or a stale workspace root).
proposals.rationale: Two reads succeeded on the same thread immediately before the failures, so the break is in the requested paths, not the reader; fixing path resolution at the source stops the repetition instead of retrying.

proposals.action: Include the requested path (and the workspace root in effect) in the Tamoz::Agent::ToolError payload and effect_attempt record for path_outside_workspace.
proposals.rationale: The repeated_failure rule correctly flags one recurring code, but without the rejected path the finding cannot be acted on; this is the single missing datum in the record.

proposals.action: Consider a bounded retry or an explicit terminal marker for deterministic validation failures like path_outside_workspace, so a repeated-failure burst is capped instead of issuing 12 identical first attempts.
proposals.rationale: All 12 failures are attempt #1 with no retry and no halt, which is correct for validation errors but let a deterministic mistake consume 12 effects in 26 ms.

Summary: Investigated the Tamoz runtime's own record for the last few hours (windows of 240 and 1440 minutes checked; they contain the same single burst). Of 42 effect attempts, the only failures are 12 tool.read_file calls on thread.noise.5, every one failing with Tamoz::Agent::ToolError code path_outside_workspace. Reads that asked for paths inside the workspace succeeded seconds earlier on the same thread, so the reader and workspace root were healthy; the 12 rejected calls requested paths that resolved outside the workspace root and the path-validation guard refused them.
Hypothesis (high confidence): path_outside_workspace
Findings:
1. Exactly one failure mode exists in the window: 12 tool.read_file effect attempts on thread.noise.5 (1791145495708–1791145495734), all class Tamoz::Agent::ToolError with code path_outside_workspace. No other error class or code appears anywhere in the record. [from probe_self_diagnose, probe_self_timeline]
2. The burst is the only activity in 24 hours: six turns (thread.noise.0–thread.noise.5) between 1791145495556 and 1791145495734, all requested and completed. Widening the probe window from 4h to 24h returns the identical record, so nothing earlier or later contributes failures. [from probe_self_timeline]
3. The diagnose probe's single high-severity finding (rule effect.repeated_failure, category dependency_unavailable) fires on exactly these 12 attempts, and degraded is false with no other findings — the runtime's own diagnosis agrees there is one recurring cause. [from probe_self_diagnose]
4. On thread.noise.5, two tool.read_file attempts immediately before the burst succeeded (task.df40fab6 at 1791145495701, task.8d5dec3d at 1791145495704), then 12 consecutive reads failed. The reader and workspace root were working seconds earlier; only the requested paths were rejected. Each failure is attempt #1 and never retried. [from probe_self_explain_turn]
5. Everything else succeeded: 18/18 model.generate.plan attempts, the 2 pre-failure reads, and 6 write_file approval decisions all resolved as approve (decision.f19ea059, 385f342f, 9f44433d, cd0f32b0, cac26ad8, 86286b83). The failures are not approval-related, and there are no unknown outcomes, timeouts, or journal drops. [from probe_self_diagnose, probe_self_explain_turn]
6. Alternative codes can be excluded by absence and by context: no timeout, rate_limit, unavailable, denied, or unknown-outcome codes occur anywhere in the 24h window, and the two successful reads on the same thread rule out a broken read path or lost workspace root. [from probe_self_diagnose, probe_self_explain_turn]
Still unknown:
- The requested path arguments of the 12 failed tool.read_file calls: The recorded effect attempts and turn decision carry only class and code, not the argument values, so the report cannot say which off-root paths were requested (absolute paths, traversal, or symlink resolution) nor which plan step generated them. The runtime record would need the call arguments logged to close this.
- The guard implementation that raises path_outside_workspace: The workspace contains no source (list_directory is empty, search for the code has no matches), so the exact resolution rules the guard applies cannot be confirmed from code; the conclusion rests on the runtime record alone.
Proposed next actions (not executed; ask for one to run it through approval):
1. Investigate what produced the off-root read paths in thread.noise.5 starting at 1791145495708: the model plans succeeded, so check whether the plan output or the caller resolved paths against the wrong base (absolute host paths or a stale workspace root).: Two reads succeeded on the same thread immediately before the failures, so the break is in the requested paths, not the reader; fixing path resolution at the source stops the repetition instead of retrying. [from probe_self_explain_turn, probe_self_timeline]
2. Include the requested path (and the workspace root in effect) in the Tamoz::Agent::ToolError payload and effect_attempt record for path_outside_workspace.: The repeated_failure rule correctly flags one recurring code, but without the rejected path the finding cannot be acted on; this is the single missing datum in the record. [from probe_self_diagnose]
3. Consider a bounded retry or an explicit terminal marker for deterministic validation failures like path_outside_workspace, so a repeated-failure burst is capped instead of issuing 12 identical first attempts.: All 12 failures are attempt #1 with no retry and no halt, which is correct for validation errors but let a deterministic mistake consume 12 effects in 26 ms. [from probe_self_diagnose]

Findings report: every finding cites a probe result from this turn. Proposals were not executed.

findings.statement: Two turns failed in the window: thread.failed.0 (request.6ce07497, execution 46961c54) and thread.failed.1 (request.9af15c33, execution 26d974a1), both status=failed with failure class unclassified and retryable=0.

Both failed executions ran graph builder-failure and went running -> failed in ~5 ms with zero effects recorded — no failed or unknown attempts — so the failure happened before any effect was executed.

Five journal worker errors with reason lease_lost were logged at 1791145495718, 13 ms before the first failed turn was requested; the journal shows documents=5, drops=0, so this evidence is intact rather than lossy.

All 30 effect attempts in the window succeeded (18 model.generate.plan, 12 tool.read_file, p95 <= 1 ms), and the healthy threads (thread.noise.*) completed with the same effect mix — the failure is isolated to the two turns that follow the lease_lost burst.

No other error source exists in the record: occurrences=0, degraded=false, and a 1440-minute lookback is identical to the 360-minute one. The string 'unclassified' is the requests table saying the failure could not be classified, and 'dependency_unavailable' is a rule category label — neither is a root-cause error code.

gaps.datum: Why the worker lost its lease (heartbeat timeout, restart, OOM, pause, clock skew)
gaps.why: The journal entries carry only reason=lease_lost with empty correlation fields; the trigger is not in the runtime record and needs worker process logs or host metrics around 1791145495718.

gaps.datum: The exception text behind the unclassified turn failures
gaps.why: The requests table stores only failure.class=unclassified with no message, so the link between lease loss and these two turns is inferential (timing, zero effects, no other error source) rather than confirmed in-band.

gaps.datum: Journal history older than the recorded window
gaps.why: The journal is lossy by design; drops=0 for this window, but a precursor event outside the 24-hour record cannot be fully excluded.

proposals.action: Inspect worker process logs and host metrics around timestamp 1791145495718 to determine why the lease was dropped (restart, OOM, pause, network partition).
proposals.rationale: The record shows that the lease was lost but not why; the trigger lives outside the runtime database.

proposals.action: Map worker lease loss to a classified failure class on affected turns (instead of unclassified) and mark it retryable where the lease can be reacquired.
proposals.rationale: Both turns failed with class unclassified and retryable=0, which hid the root cause from the diagnosis rules and blocked automatic retry.

proposals.action: Add an alert on bursts of tamoz.worker.error with reason=lease_lost.
proposals.rationale: The 5-error burst preceded both turn failures and is the earliest visible signal of the incident.

report.summary: Asked to find the root cause of a runtime incident in the last few hours using the self-probes. Two turns (thread.failed.0 and thread.failed.1, graph builder-failure) ended failed ~5 ms after starting with zero effect attempts, immediately after a burst of five journal worker errors with reason lease_lost; every other turn in the window completed with all 30 effects succeeding, and no other error source exists in 24 hours. The record points to worker lease loss as the root cause, with the turn-level failure recorded only as class "unclassified".

Summary: Asked to find the root cause of the Tamoz runtime incident in the last few hours. The 24h probe window contains exactly six turns (thread.noise.0-5) that all completed normally; after the last turn ended, a post-turn batch produced 8 tool.read_file effects that failed once each with not_found (high-severity noise), and one external MCP effect (tool.mcp.ponds.set_aerator) was left with an unknown outcome after a transport timeout. The only unresolved, state-changing anomaly is the aerator effect.
Hypothesis (medium confidence): transport_timeout
Findings:
1. All six turns (thread.noise.0 through .5, graph builder-turn) completed normally: 30 effects succeeded, including 12 in-turn tool.read_file successes and 18/18 model.generate.plan, and every write_file approval was asked and approved (decisions 8b8313bd, 143aea32, 8f464b5e, ad14aa3c, 8ddf5202, 870e8a4a). The incident is not inside the turns themselves. [from probe_self_diagnose, probe_self_timeline, probe_self_explain_turn]
2. After the last turn completed (thread.noise.5 at ms 1791145918117), a post-turn batch created 8 tool.read_file effects between ms 1791145918130 and 1791145918145 that each failed on attempt #1 with Tamoz::Agent::ToolError / not_found and were never retried (no attempt #2 anywhere). Distribution: two each on thread.noise.0/.1/.2, one each on .3/.4, none on .5. Note each thread's two batch reads have distinct effect keys and task ids, unlike the identical repeats the in-turn reads show per thread. [from probe_self_timeline, probe_self_diagnose, probe_self_explain_turn]
3. The runtime's effect.repeated_failure rule (severity high, category dependency_unavailable) fired on that not_found cluster (count 8), but not_found on a read-only tool is a terminal client-side error (target path does not exist), not a dependency outage: nothing was scheduled for retry, no turn failed, and all other reads succeeded. This cluster is noise relative to the critical anomaly. [from probe_self_diagnose]
4. The critical anomaly is effect sha256:a7042f1e... on tool.mcp.ponds.set_aerator (thread.noise.5, execution d2a87dc7-9dff-4eb1-8bc7-0e35ff48ed02, task.3667ee96): status unknown, failure Tamoz::MCP::TransportError / transport_timeout at ms 1791145918147-148, flagged by rule effect.outcome_unknown at severity critical. It is an external, state-changing side effect whose real-world outcome (aerator on or off) cannot be determined from the record, so it is waiting for human reconciliation via `tamoz resolve`. [from probe_self_diagnose, probe_self_explain_turn]
5. The two failure clusters are independent rather than causal: the last not_found read failure (ms ...145) precedes the transport timeout (ms ...147-148), they come from different subsystems (Tamoz::Agent::ToolError in the agent tool layer vs Tamoz::MCP::TransportError in the MCP transport), and the turn involved (thread.noise.5) had already completed successfully at ms ...117. Chronology rules out the timeout wedging the executor, and no evidence links the failed reads to the MCP call. [from probe_self_timeline, probe_self_diagnose]
Still unknown:
- The record stores no arguments for the 8 failed tool.read_file effects, so their exact target paths are unknown.: It would distinguish a stale replay or canary manifest from a workspace regression; the empty workspace is consistent with not_found but unconfirmed.
- The actual state of the pond aerator in the external system is not in the record (that is what status=unknown means).: The reconciliation direction for `tamoz resolve` (applied vs not applied) must come from the source system, not from these probes.
- The occurrences table has 0 rows and the journal is empty, so there is no worker error log beyond the effect failures.: A worker crash underlying the burst would have appeared there; its absence supports the two-independent-causes reading but is negative evidence only.
Proposed next actions (not executed; ask for one to run it through approval):
1. Check the pond's real aerator state in the external system, then settle effect sha256:a7042f1eea66d83c6d12160fab6ca25cef1569f3f0f69e545b982b46dc7d194f with `tamoz resolve`. Do not resubmit set_aerator before settling it.: It is the only effect with an unknown outcome on a state-changing external system; blind retries risk double-actuating the aerator. [from probe_self_diagnose, probe_self_explain_turn]
2. If the post-turn read batch is a scheduled replay or canary, fix or remove its manifest paths: all 8 reads missed on the first attempt and nothing was rescheduled.: Treats the effect.repeated_failure rule as noise from stale paths rather than a live dependency problem, so it is fixed once instead of retried. [from probe_self_diagnose, probe_self_timeline]
3. No action needed on the six turns themselves.: All completed with approvals recorded and no model-side failures. [from probe_self_timeline]
